guideline: Categorize errors into types: E1 (ignorance of theorem), E2 (wrong formula/algorithm), E3 (minor calculation mistakes)
Humans were asked to solve the selected questions and their answers were compared to the ground‑truth answers.

We pick GPT4, ChatGPT and Alpaca to understand their error sources. We include the following error types: (E1) the model does not even know this theorem, (E2) the model does know the theorem, but uses the wrong formula or algorithm, (E3) the model knows the theorem and the formula, the error is only caused by minor calculation mistakes.

changes_made.explanation: Simplified guideline to core error categorization framework. Normalized criteria from error codes (E1/E2/E3) to descriptive criteria names. Removed duplicated/extraneous items from criteria list.

overall_notes: The paper focuses on evaluating NLG capabilities for theorem-based question answering. Extraction was generally accurate but needed normalization of model names (removed duplicates/variants) and clarification that ChatGPT is used for post-generation evaluation (answer span extraction), changing Q3 answer from No to Yes. The primary contribution is TheoremQA benchmark evaluation with both automatic metrics and human error analysis.
